nodes.label: FlatAim Load-Order Fix: Restore save-0.sav Order, Drop sshock2ee Requirement
nodes.rationale: Restored save-0.sav so FlatAim's KPF loads after sshock2ee and dropped its requirements=["sshock2ee"] dependency, reversing an earlier bottom-last assumption. The change matched the last known-good manual test instruction and removed a possible AE dependency-load blocker.

nodes.label: Package FlatAim KPF as ZIP/PK for KEX Mounting
nodes.rationale: Diagnosed FlatAim's F5 failure as a package-mount-format bug: the KPF began with raw sq_scripts bytes instead of a ZIP 'PK' header, so KEX never mounted kpf:/mods/flataim/. Repacking as a proper ZIP/PK archive was prioritized over further load-order or DLL changes.

nodes.label: Try Native Cursor Globals for FlatAim Crosshair
nodes.rationale: With the Squirrel bridge proven live, tried writing the FlatAim reticle position into KEX's native cursor globals as the least-invasive way to move the original crosshair, keeping the topmost Win32 overlay disabled by default. This was a diagnostic probe, not yet a confirmed fix.

nodes.label: Keep Weapon CameraObj Controller-Local, HMD Roll Only
nodes.rationale: Stopped converting the visible weapon CameraObj through HMD app/body rotation after it caused the gun to drag with head yaw; kept the model controller-local and applied only HMD roll correction. Accepted a small increase in visible-model smoothing for weapon weight.

nodes.label: Use Funk Custom for Standalone Left-Hand Mesh Exports
nodes.rationale: Added a separate Funk Custom export path that builds a fresh single-subobject LGMD from a snapshotted Max mesh, rather than reusing the brittle legacy BSP route or emptying an animated weapon LGMD into a faux hand asset. Funk Direct/Funk Mesh remained the conservative paths for edits that must preserve original subobject/joint identity.

nodes.label: Broaden Viewmodel/World-Depth Probe Before Depth-Write Spike
nodes.rationale: Kept viewmodel/world-depth work log-only and added tracking of the UAV-capable OMSetRenderTargetsAndUnorderedAccessViews path, because the initial clear hook fired but scene-depth remember state stayed empty. Required pointer-match proof rather than same-size/same-format guesses before any future behavioral write.

nodes.label: Viewmodel/World-Depth Runtime Seam Confirmed
nodes.rationale: Runtime logs proved the exact depth seam across two captures: KEX clears the remembered world-depth DSV at a fixed draw index, and the viewmodel draw cluster begins immediately after. This unlocked moving from log-only classification to a guarded visual depth-preservation spike.

nodes.label: Build Default-Off Viewmodel/World-Depth Visual Spike
nodes.rationale: Added the first behavioral viewmodel/world-depth test gated behind viewmodel_depth_visual_spike=false, preserving remembered world depth only for pointer-matched clears and restoring native RT/DSV state after each draw. Explicitly not to ship as a baseline feature until headset testing ruled out weapon disappearance or postprocess corruption.

nodes.label: Expand Funk Custom Toward General LGMD Object Support
nodes.rationale: Expanded Funk Custom into a general fresh-asset LGMD path supporting multiple mesh subobjects, editable vhot helpers, rebuilt material names, and one-click KPF packaging, while keeping Funk Direct/Funk Mesh untouched for weapon edits. LGMM/.CAL skinned-skeleton work was deliberately deferred to a later tier.

nodes.label: Treat First ss2vr_lh Tint as Material/Shader Issue
nodes.rationale: Treated the transparent/bluish look of the first custom left-hand export as a material/shader issue rather than a material-ID mapping bug, since parser inspection showed correct resolution to ND-arm.psd via the viewmodel invis/fill/rim material chain. The next planned test was a deliberate opaque material override, not a material-index change.

nodes.label: Stop Using Cursor Globals for FlatAim's Visible Crosshair
nodes.rationale: Rejected KEX cursor globals as the visible-crosshair driver after v0.4 proved writes/readback moved but the on-screen crosshair stayed centered; re-confirmed rejection of the topmost Win32 overlay and opaque-cover paths. Future crosshair movement was redirected toward native Shock overlay/draw ownership.

nodes.label: Draw FlatAim's Moving Crosshair Through ShockOverlay
nodes.rationale: Chose to draw FlatAim's moving crosshair through the native Squirrel/AE HUD path (ShockOverlay.DrawBitmap of the stock crosshai bitmap) instead of a new OS/D3D hook, based on a user-identified draw EID and old Shock source confirming overlay-22 ownership. Expected to compose better with game UI/menus than the rejected topmost overlay.

nodes.label: Import SS2VR Lessons into FlatAim Local Docs
nodes.rationale: Created flataim/docs/SS2VR_FINDINGS.md to import SS2VR's semantic selection, deferred projectile redirect, CameraObj domain split, Shock overlay crosshair, and ZIP/PK packaging lessons into FlatAim, since the sidequest kept re-hitting failure families the mainline project had already characterized.

nodes.label: Give FlatAim Its Own Local Memory Pack
nodes.rationale: Gave FlatAim its own local memory pack (CURRENT_STATE.md, FAILURE_REGISTRY.md, implementation map) under flataim/docs/ instead of relying on the large cross-project SS2VR logs, because flataim/README.md had grown stale and easy to misuse as current truth.

nodes.label: Depth-Limit Interaction Beam from Selected-Object Marker
nodes.rationale: Added the first interaction-beam depth stop using UI hit distance then the selected-object marker/depth, deliberately avoiding a generic world/BSP wall raycast gate because broad collision hits had previously risked re-breaking flush switch/card controls.

nodes.label: Use Roomscale Capsule Clamp as First Wall-Safety Layer
nodes.rationale: Added a default-off horizontal roomscale HMD clamp (wall_safety_enabled) limiting only x/z RenderView translation, treating it as a reversible comfort spike rather than a full wall-polygon solver, since KEX collision owns the body but injected 6DOF can visually push the head through walls.

nodes.label: Treat Pose-Bridge KISS as Staged Validation, Not Immediate Rewrite
nodes.rationale: Chose to validate the cheap live/config hypothesis (disabling model_pose_compensate_hmd_rotation) before committing to a full Option-B pose-bridge rewrite, keeping right-hand projectile/world aim raw and separate from visible CameraObj cleanup pending that test's result.

nodes.label: Prove Native Shock HUD Layout Ownership with Guarded Rect-Write Spike
nodes.rationale: Added a default-off, INI-gated spike that rewrites the native gOverlayRects[50] layout table only after validating the confirmed gOverlayOrder[50] signature, to prove layout ownership before investing in a final floating-panel VR HUD architecture.

nodes.label: Clear FlatAim Aim State on Startup Before Trusting Reticle Position
nodes.rationale: Treated ss2fa_aim as stale unless both DLL and Squirrel explicitly clear/republish it after load, because stale valid state surviving a save/load was a more likely explanation for post-load crosshair offset than a regression in the reticle draw math.

nodes.label: Keep Selected-Object Beam Clipping Separate from Wall/Floor Depth Clipping
nodes.rationale: Confirmed pointer_depth_clip is validated only for selected/frobbable object markers and explicitly refused to stretch it into a wall/floor/window/table solution, keeping arbitrary-geometry clipping as a separate future layer using preserved world depth or native collision.

nodes.label: Do Not Capture Native Overlay Rect Originals from a Zero Table
nodes.rationale: Required validating usable kOverlayInv/kOverlayAmmo/kOverlayMeters anchor rects before capturing the original gOverlayRects table, after an early capture from an all-zero table collapsed the HUD to the top-left corner.

nodes.label: FlatAim v0.11 Exposes Semantic Target and Clears Stale Native Hover
nodes.rationale: Treated ss2fa_hl=0 and staleness as explicit native-target clears rather than no-ops after finding the DLL only ever wrote positive semantic targets into native hover/frob globals; added a projected debug marker to compare visible reticle, semantic target, and native inspector state.

nodes.label: FlatAim Selection Should Be Screen-Projected Semantic Scoring
nodes.rationale: Made screen-projected semantic scoring (distance from WorldToScreen position to the drawn reticle) FlatAim's default object-selection basis after the world-ray cylinder selector picked objects far from the crosshair depending on approach angle; kept the old selector only as an A/B diagnostic.

nodes.label: Stabilize Squirrel Highlight Targets Before VR Bracket Rendering
nodes.rationale: Kept the C++ rule that VR brackets consume only Squirrel's ss2vr_hl target (never falling back to KEX's raw objectUnderCursor), and added a Squirrel-side target-quality/noise/latch filter after logs showed ss2vr_hl itself flickering across noisy and helper-like objects.

nodes.label: Rect-Rearrange Spike Should Transform All Usable Overlay Rects by Band
nodes.rationale: Changed the HUD rect-rearrange proof to transform every usable gOverlayRects entry by vertical band instead of moving only a few named panels, after testing showed late AE-era buttons/icons went missing or out of sync when only Inv/Ammo/Meters were moved.

nodes.label: Item Physics Moves Only Through a Left-Grip, Whitelist-Gated Lane
nodes.rationale: Shipped the first moving-object physics build as default-off and Squirrel-gated behind a whitelist (helper/CameraObj rejection, BlockFrob rejection, size cap, allow-list) on a separate left-grip lane from the left-trigger frob lane, since a Stage 0 logger proved 'has physics' alone was not a safe movement permission for large objects like tables.

nodes.label: FlatAim Bracket Visuals Split Native-Looking Feedback from True Native Handoff
nodes.rationale: Split native-looking bracket feedback (stock BRACK0-3 bitmaps drawn by FlatAim) from true native bracket handoff, which was left unsolved pending an observational, INI-revertible probe of the FUN_1404b9a80 detour that must call through unchanged while disabled.

nodes.label: Fine-Tooth Cleanup Checkpoint and Quiet Baseline
nodes.rationale: Tagged a git checkpoint and backed up the live INI before removing two documented dead-end paths (native-stereo byte forcing, snap/direct-yaw writer) from live code, keeping all confirmed working routes quiet by default and adding MkDocs as the project's browsable docs spine.

nodes.label: Pose-Loss Viewmodel Fallback and Black Menu Background
nodes.rationale: On tracking loss, stopped writing SS2VR CameraObj overrides so the native Nightdive handler resumes the standard viewmodel pose, and hid/destroyed the additive left-hand model, after users reported weapons/hands sticking inside the HMD when the old Squirrel fallback kept stale VR offsets.

nodes.label: Keep Current State as a Dashboard, Move Build History Out
nodes.rationale: Narrowed CURRENT_STATE.md to only the active baseline/build/next-tests dashboard and moved release hashes and older handoff notes into BUILD_HISTORY.md, because the always-read entry point had accumulated the same long history that belonged in domain docs and the decision log.

nodes.label: Add Preserved-Subobject Hand Extraction Before More Fresh Hand Recompiles
nodes.rationale: Added a Funk Extract path that isolates and preserves the known-good pistol hand's source material/UV/light/normal/face records and BSP slice instead of regenerating them, after comparing the known-good hand (265 faces/186 lights) against a fresh Funk Custom export (358 faces/1074 light records) as a cleaner test of the blue/translucent tint cause.

nodes.label: Lock Pose Bridge Fixes Behind Paired DLL/Squirrel Diagnostics
nodes.rationale: Stopped tuning the weapon/hand pose bridge by headset appearance alone and required paired DLL (pose_diag_right/left) and Squirrel ([SS2VR-POSE]) diagnostics so a bug could be localized to C++ publication, Squirrel consumption, or AE rendering, using the left-hand viewmodel as a parity check.

nodes.label: FlatAim Visible Weapon Uses Screen-Local Mode-4 Diagnostic
nodes.rationale: Stopped treating weapon_follow_mode=3 as a fix for pitch-look causing weapon roll and added mode 4, a screen-local diagnostic canceling KEX's pitched CameraObj basis via Heading=rawHeading/safeCos and pitch-aware Bank compensation.

nodes.label: FlatAim Mode Numbers Must Pass C++ Clamp and Squirrel Proof
nodes.rationale: Established that any new FlatAim numeric follow-mode must update the C++ LoadIni() validation clamp in the same change as the Squirrel implementation, after a stale 1..3 clamp silently reset a staged mode 4 back to mode 1, invalidating a full round of roll testing.

nodes.label: Retire FlatAim Inverse-Cos Bank Cancellation
nodes.rationale: Retired the inverse-cos Heading boost plus Bank cancellation as the mode-4 solution after it produced a >360-degree gun roll and pitch inversion near vertical camera pitch, replacing it with a bounded hybrid that fades Heading near vertical and uses lateral CameraObj.Offset instead.

nodes.label: FlatAim v0.17 Uses Bounded Anti-Roll, Not Inverse-Cos
nodes.rationale: Added Bank cancellation derived only from the already-faded v0.16 Heading term (no cos-division) to address remaining mid-pitch roll that the bounded hybrid alone did not fully remove, without reintroducing the v0.15 singularity.

nodes.label: FlatAim Visible Weapon Pivots to Rig-Level aimPoint
nodes.rationale: Stopped treating final CameraObj Heading/Pitch/Bank tuning as the main fix after bounded Bank cancellation showed no meaningful improvement, moving to mode 5: inserting FlatAim yaw/pitch at the native viewmodel rig's aimPoint before the stock gunPoint-to-CameraObj write runs.

nodes.label: FlatAim Stops Treating Rig-Level aimPoint as the Roll Fix
nodes.rationale: Falsified rig-level aimPoint insertion (mode 5) after logs proved it ran but roll/slide symptoms persisted, and source review showed ND.PointRig only linearly adds Euler channels; moved to mode 6, a bounded screen-axis Heading/Bank decomposition with rotation locks off.

nodes.label: Separate Tracked and Fallback Weapon Viewmodel Scale
nodes.rationale: Split the single ss2vr_weapon_scale into separate tracked and fallback scale values after the native-KEX-frame remap made the old 0.65 value feel too small while tracked but far too large in native fallback pose, since apparent scale became pose-mode dependent.

nodes.label: FlatAim Exits Final CameraObj Euler Tuning for the Weapon-Roll Test
nodes.rationale: Abandoned final CameraObj Euler-channel tuning entirely after mode-6 variant 0 still routed near-vertical horizontal aim into Bank, moving to mode 7: hiding the native CameraObj weapon while F5 is active and driving a transient world-space proxy weapon along the FlatAim ray instead.

nodes.label: FlatAim World Proxy Uses Object.Teleport Facing Order
nodes.rationale: Determined world-object Object.Teleport/Position facing order is (roll, pitch, yaw), not CameraObj's Heading/Pitch/Bank, after the mode-7 proxy showed yaw fixed to world north; replaced unreliable CameraObj Draw?=false hiding with reversible tiny-scale hiding, confirmed via Nightdive's PointRig.GetPhysicsVector() convention.

nodes.label: CameraObj Native-Frame Remap Is Orientation-Only
nodes.rationale: Applied the native pre-override KEX camera frame remap to visible CameraObj orientation only, not translation, after using it for translation caused apparent scale/depth errors (early table clipping, undersized models) even though it had fixed HMD yaw/roll bleed in orientation.

nodes.label: FlatAim v0.22 Proxy Uses Screen-Up Look-At as Diagnostic Default
nodes.rationale: Kept mode 7 active but replaced the plain (roll,pitch,yaw) proxy comparator with facing mode 4: aiming the proxy at a target on the FlatAim ray and deriving Roll from camera/screen-up, after plain channel-swap testing still turned pitched horizontal aim into roll.

nodes.label: FlatAim v0.23 Treats Screen-Up Proxy Roll Sign as Unproven
nodes.rationale: Accepted that scalar Heading/Bank redistribution was the wrong family of fix for the native CameraObj path, kept the world-proxy approach, but treated v0.22's screen-up Roll sign as unproven and added a signed A/B test plus rollRaw/rollApplied/rollSign logging after users still saw roll while aimed up/down.

nodes.label: FlatAim v0.24 Tests Proxy-Origin Look-At with Zero Dynamic Roll
nodes.rationale: Treated the dynamic screen-up Roll term itself as suspect and added facing mode 5: proxy-origin look-at direction combined with world-object (bank, pitch, heading) and zero per-frame Roll solve, isolating whether the look-at geometry or the dynamic Roll computation was the remaining problem.

nodes.label: Snap-Turn v2 Uses Accumulator/Body Transport Plus Immediate Display Yaw Step
nodes.rationale: Reintroduced snap turn on top of KEX's normal mouse-accumulator body transport rather than reviving previously-rejected direct/absolute-angle writers, updating the cached HMD-authoritative display baseline immediately by an expected yaw delta and suppressing post-snap HMD deltas for 180ms to avoid stacking head motion into the snap.

nodes.label: Default-Off Gating for Behavioral/Safety Diagnostics
nodes.rationale: Recurring rule across the depth-visual spike, HUD rect-rearrange spike, phys-grab lane, and wall-safety clamp: ship a new behavioral or safety-affecting change first as an INI-gated, default-off diagnostic with an explicit success/failure log gate, not as a baseline feature.

nodes.label: Scalar CameraObj Euler Tuning Rejected as a Fix Family
nodes.rationale: After FlatAim modes 3 through 6 all failed to fix pitch-driven weapon roll, concluded that scalar tuning of final CameraObj Heading/Pitch/Bank/Euler channels is not the right fix family for pitch-invariant screen-local weapon aim. Further work moved to a different representation (rig-level, then world-space proxy) instead of sign-flipping more scalars.

nodes.label: Keep Interaction/Rendering Domains From Bleeding Into Each Other
nodes.rationale: Recurring convention: keep distinct domains separate — selected-object beam clipping vs. wall/floor depth clipping, physical grab vs. frob interaction, visible CameraObj orientation vs. translation/aim — rather than solving one problem by overloading another domain's data path.
